title: Rigveda 1.91: To Soma
source: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (undated (catalogued with Penn's 18th-19th c. Vedic manuscripts)), OPenn, Public Domain Mark + Aufrecht's accented text (GRETIL) + Griffith's English (VedaWeb)
description: Rigveda 1.91: To Soma: Sanskrit text and Griffith's English, each verse linked to the page of an undated Rigveda manuscript (Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41) that carries it.
introduction:
Rigveda 1.91 is a hymn of 23 verses addressed to Soma. It stands in book (maṇḍala) 1, a collection of hymns by many families of poets. The Rigveda is the oldest collection of Sanskrit hymns, composed in the second half of the second millennium BCE and handed down orally for many centuries before it was written down.

The manuscript shown is Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (University of Pennsylvania), an undated paper manuscript of the padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text, in which every word is written separately and compounds are split) of the whole Ṛgveda in Devanāgarī, 884 leaves in fascicles, 7-9 lines to the page, accents in red; this hymn stands on fol. 61v-63r. Each section below gives the verses that end on one page; the page boundaries were read on the images (the opening words of every page), not counted out. Where the manuscript is a padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text), the section shows Aufrecht's continuous (saṃhitā) text first and, as the edition text, the padapāṭha of the same verses, which is the form written on the page.
translator_notes: Sanskrit: Aufrecht's edition (1877) with the Vedic accents, as entered by van Nooten and Holland (GRETIL).

English: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda (1889-1892; 2nd ed. 1896-1897), from the VedaWeb digital text; OCR slips in that text were corrected against the printed 2nd edition (data/sources/rigveda/griffith_errata.json).

translation.original_ref: RV 1.91.1-2 (aṣṭaka 1, adhyāya 6, varga 19); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 61v
translation.original_text:
1tvaṁ so̍ma̱ pra ci̍kito manī̱ṣā tvaṁ raji̍ṣṭha̱m anu̍ neṣi̱ panthā̍m | tava̱ praṇī̍tī pi̱taro̍ na indo de̱veṣu̱ ratna̍m abhajanta̱ dhīrā̍ḥ ||
2tvaṁ so̍ma̱ kratu̍bhiḥ su̱kratu̍r bhū̱s tvaṁ dakṣai̍ḥ su̱dakṣo̍ vi̱śvave̍dāḥ | tvaṁ vṛṣā̍ vṛṣa̱tvebhi̍r mahi̱tvā dyu̱mnebhi̍r dyu̱mny a̍bhavo nṛ̱cakṣā̍ḥ ||
translation.text:
1Thou, Soma, art preeminent for wisdom; along the straightest path thou art our leader. Our wise forefathers by thy guidance, Indu, dealt out among the Gods their share of treasure.
2Thou by thine insight art most wise, O Soma, strong by thine energies and all possessing, Mighty art thou by all thy powers and greatness, by glories art thou glorious, guide of mortals.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 61v (OPenn image 63, upper leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 1.90.5 ‹uta naḥ dhiyaḥ go--agrāḥ›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 62r, begins in RV 1.91.3 ‹-asi soma›. Verses 1.91.1-2 end on this page.

2tvam | soma | kratu-bhiḥ | su-kratuḥ | bhūḥ | tvam | dakṣaiḥ | su-dakṣaḥ | viśva-vedāḥ | tvam | vṛṣā | vṛṣa-tvebhiḥ | mahi-tvā | dyumnebhiḥ | dyumnī | abhavaḥ | nṛ-cakṣāḥ

translation.original_ref: RV 1.91.3-12 (aṣṭaka 1, adhyāya 6, varga 19); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 62r
translation.original_text:
3rājño̱ nu te̱ varu̍ṇasya vra̱tāni̍ bṛ̱had ga̍bhī̱raṁ tava̍ soma̱ dhāma̍ | śuci̱ṣ ṭvam a̍si pri̱yo na mi̱tro da̱kṣāyyo̍ arya̱mevā̍si soma ||
4yā te̱ dhāmā̍ni di̱vi yā pṛ̍thi̱vyāṁ yā parva̍te̱ṣv oṣa̍dhīṣv a̱psu | tebhi̍r no̱ viśvai̍ḥ su̱manā̱ ahe̍ḻa̱n rāja̍n soma̱ prati̍ ha̱vyā gṛ̍bhāya ||
5tvaṁ so̍māsi̱ satpa̍ti̱s tvaṁ rājo̱ta vṛ̍tra̱hā | tvam bha̱dro a̍si̱ kratu̍ḥ ||
6tvaṁ ca̍ soma no̱ vaśo̍ jī̱vātu̱ṁ na ma̍rāmahe | pri̱yasto̍tro̱ vana̱spati̍ḥ ||
7tvaṁ so̍ma ma̱he bhaga̱ṁ tvaṁ yūna̍ ṛtāya̱te | dakṣa̍ṁ dadhāsi jī̱vase̍ ||
8tvaṁ na̍ḥ soma vi̱śvato̱ rakṣā̍ rājann aghāya̱taḥ | na ri̍ṣye̱t tvāva̍ta̱ḥ sakhā̍ ||
9soma̱ yās te̍ mayo̱bhuva̍ ū̱taya̱ḥ santi̍ dā̱śuṣe̍ | tābhi̍r no 'vi̱tā bha̍va ||
10i̱maṁ ya̱jñam i̱daṁ vaco̍ jujuṣā̱ṇa u̱pāga̍hi | soma̱ tvaṁ no̍ vṛ̱dhe bha̍va ||
11soma̍ gī̱rbhiṣ ṭvā̍ va̱yaṁ va̱rdhayā̍mo vaco̱vida̍ḥ | su̱mṛ̱ḻī̱ko na̱ ā vi̍śa ||
12ga̱ya̱sphāno̍ amīva̱hā va̍su̱vit pu̍ṣṭi̱vardha̍naḥ | su̱mi̱traḥ so̍ma no bhava ||
translation.text:
3Thine are King Varuṇa's eternal statutes, lofty and deep, O Soma, is thy glory. All-pure art thou like Mitra the beloved, adorable, like Aryaman, O Soma.
4With all thy glories on the earth, in heaven, on mountains, in the plants, and in the waters,– With all of these, well-pleased and not in anger, accept, O royal Soma, our oblations.
5Thou, Soma, art the Lord of heroes, King, yea, Vr̥itra-slayer thou: Thou art auspicious energy.
6And, Soma, let it be thy wish that we may live and may not die: Praise-loving Lord of plants art thou.
7To him who keeps the law, both old and young, thou givest happiness, And energy that he may live.
8Guard us, King Soma, on all sides from him who threatens us: never let The friend of one like thee be harmed.
9With those delightful aids which thou hast, Soma, for the worshipper,– Even with those protect thou us.
10Accepting this our sacrifice and this our praise, O Soma, come, And be thou nigh to prosper us.
11Well-skilled in speech we magnify thee, Soma, with our sacred songs: Come thou to us, most gracious One.
12Enricher, healer of disease, wealth-finder, prospering our store, Be, Soma, a good Friend to us.

translation.original_ref: RV 1.91.13-19 (aṣṭaka 1, adhyāya 6, varga 21); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 62v
translation.original_text:
13soma̍ rāra̱ndhi no̍ hṛ̱di gāvo̱ na yava̍se̱ṣv ā | marya̍ iva̱ sva o̱kye̍ ||
14yaḥ so̍ma sa̱khye tava̍ rā̱raṇa̍d deva̱ martya̍ḥ | taṁ dakṣa̍ḥ sacate ka̱viḥ ||
15u̱ru̱ṣyā ṇo̍ a̱bhiśa̍ste̱ḥ soma̱ ni pā̱hy aṁha̍saḥ | sakhā̍ su̱śeva̍ edhi naḥ ||
16ā pyā̍yasva̱ sam e̍tu te vi̱śvata̍ḥ soma̱ vṛṣṇya̍m | bhavā̱ vāja̍sya saṁga̱the ||
17ā pyā̍yasva madintama̱ soma̱ viśve̍bhir a̱ṁśubhi̍ḥ | bhavā̍ naḥ su̱śrava̍stama̱ḥ sakhā̍ vṛ̱dhe ||
18saṁ te̱ payā̍ṁsi̱ sam u̍ yantu̱ vājā̱ḥ saṁ vṛṣṇyā̍ny abhimāti̱ṣāha̍ḥ | ā̱pyāya̍māno a̱mṛtā̍ya soma di̱vi śravā̍ṁsy utta̱māni̍ dhiṣva ||
19yā te̱ dhāmā̍ni ha̱viṣā̱ yaja̍nti̱ tā te̱ viśvā̍ pari̱bhūr a̍stu ya̱jñam | ga̱ya̱sphāna̍ḥ pra̱tara̍ṇaḥ su̱vīro 'vī̍rahā̱ pra ca̍rā soma̱ duryā̍n ||
translation.text:
13Soma, be happy in our heart, as milch-kine in the grassy meads, As a young man in his own house.
14O Soma, God, the mortal man who in thy friendship hath delight, Him doth the mighty Sage befriend.
15Save us from slanderous reproach, keep us., O Soma, from distress: Be unto us a gracious Friend.
16Soma, wax great. From every side may vigorous powers unite in thee: Be in the gathering-place of strength.
17Wax, O most gladdening Soma, great through all thy rays of light, and be A Friend of most illustrious fame t6 prosper us.
18In thee be juicy nutriments united, and powers and mighty foe-subduing vigour, Waxing to immortality, O Soma: win highest glories for thyself in heaven.
19Such of thy glories as with poured oblations men honour, may they all invest our worship. Wealth-giver, furtherer with troops of heroes, sparing the brave, come, Soma, to our houses.

translation.original_ref: RV 1.91.20-23 (aṣṭaka 1, adhyāya 6, varga 22); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 63r
translation.original_text:
20somo̍ dhe̱nuṁ somo̱ arva̍ntam ā̱śuṁ somo̍ vī̱raṁ ka̍rma̱ṇya̍ṁ dadāti | sā̱da̱nya̍ṁ vida̱thya̍ṁ sa̱bheya̍m pitṛ̱śrava̍ṇa̱ṁ yo dadā̍śad asmai ||
21aṣā̍ḻhaṁ yu̱tsu pṛta̍nāsu̱ papri̍ṁ sva̱rṣām a̱psāṁ vṛ̱jana̍sya go̱pām | bha̱re̱ṣu̱jāṁ su̍kṣi̱tiṁ su̱śrava̍sa̱ṁ jaya̍nta̱ṁ tvām anu̍ madema soma ||
22tvam i̱mā oṣa̍dhīḥ soma̱ viśvā̱s tvam a̱po a̍janaya̱s tvaṁ gāḥ | tvam ā ta̍tantho̱rv a1̱̍ntari̍kṣa̱ṁ tvaṁ jyoti̍ṣā̱ vi tamo̍ vavartha ||
23de̱vena̍ no̱ mana̍sā deva soma rā̱yo bhā̱gaṁ sa̍hasāvann a̱bhi yu̍dhya | mā tvā ta̍na̱d īśi̍ṣe vī̱rya̍syo̱bhaye̍bhya̱ḥ pra ci̍kitsā̱ gavi̍ṣṭau ||
translation.text:
20To him who worships Soma gives the milchcow, a fleet steed and a man of active knowledge, Skilled in home duties, meet for holy synod, for council meet, a glory to his father.
21Invincible in fight, saver in battles, guard of our camp, winner of light and water, Born amid hymns, well-housed, exceeding famous, victor, in thee will we rejoice, O Soma.
22These herbs, these milch-kine, and these running waters, all these, O Soma, thou hast generated. The spacious firmament hast thou expanded, and with the light thou hast dispelled the darkness.
23Do thou, God Soma, with thy Godlike spirit, victorious, win for us a share of riches. Let none prevent thee: thou art Lord of valour. Provide for both sides in the fray for booty.
